paraphrase: Longer recension frame: at Rājagṛha on the Vulture Peak the Buddha enters the samādhi called 'perception of the profound'; Śāriputra, through the Buddha's power, asks Avalokiteśvara how a son or daughter of good family who wishes to course in the deep perfection of wisdom should train; Avalokiteśvara answers that one should see the five aggregates as empty of own-being.

paraphrase: The Buddha rises from samādhi and approves Avalokiteśvara: 'Well said! So it is; the deep perfection of wisdom is to be practiced as you have taught; the Tathāgatas rejoice.'

paraphrase: Here, Śāriputra, form is emptiness and emptiness is form; emptiness is not other than form, form not other than emptiness; what is form is emptiness, what is emptiness is form. So too feeling, perception, formations and consciousness (s5).

location.section: shorter recension, sentence s6; Vaidya p. 97; T251 848c10-12

paraphrase: All dharmas have the mark of emptiness: unborn, unceasing, not stained, not stainless, not deficient, not complete. Therefore in emptiness there is no form, feeling, perception, formations or consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind; no forms, sounds, smells, tastes, touchables, dharmas; no eye-element up to no mind-element.

paraphrase: Relying on the perfection of wisdom the bodhisattva dwells without obstruction of mind; having no obstruction he is unafraid, has passed beyond inversions and reaches final nirvāṇa; relying on it all buddhas of the three times fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.
